The '''RG-31 Nyala''' is a [[Four-wheel drive|4×4]] multi-purpose [[Mine-Resistant Ambush Protected Vehicle]] manufactured in [[South Africa]] by [[Land Systems OMC]] (a division of [[Denel]] SOC LTD), located in [[Benoni, Gauteng|Benoni]], South Africa and in [[Turkey]] by [[FNSS Defence Systems]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.todayszaman.com/newsDetail_openPrintPage.action?newsId=120473|title=Today's Zaman, Turkish daily news|access-date=5 November 2014|archive-date=5 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305024204/http://www.todayszaman.com/newsDetail_openPrintPage.action?newsId=120473|url-status=dead}}</ref>  It is based on the [[Mamba APC]] of TFM Industries.

The RG-31 has become the multi-purpose vehicle of choice of the [[UN]] and other peacekeeping and security forces. It is finding favour with non-governmental organisations requiring a vehicle with a non-aggressive appearance to protect their personnel against [[land mine]]s.{{citation needed|date=February 2011}}

==Design==
The RG-31 is based on a [[Unimog|UNIMOG]] chassis.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Deutsche Rüstungsexporte: Einzelansicht |url=http://ruestungsexport-info.de/no_cache/de/datenbank/einzelansicht.html?tx_ruestungsexport_ruestungsexporte%5Bpage%5D=2&tx_ruestungsexport_ruestungsexporte%5Bfilter%5D%5Bland%5D=&tx_ruestungsexport_ruestungsexporte%5Bfilter%5D%5Bcategory%5D=15&tx_ruestungsexport_ruestungsexporte%5Bfilter%5D%5Bunternehmen%5D=&tx_ruestungsexport_ruestungsexporte%5Bfilter%5D%5Bsearchword%5D=&tx_ruestungsexport_ruestungsexporte%5Baction%5D=show&tx_ruestungsexport_ruestungsexporte%5Bcontroller%5D=Einzelgeschaeft&cHash=1d6da5a888dd691eca7786f56115b738&tx_ruestungsexport_ruestungsexporte%5Beinzelgeschaeft%5D=2435 |access-date=2024-06-09 |website=ruestungsexport-info.de}}</ref> It is built from a [[V-hull|V-shaped]] all-steel welded armor monocoque hull and high suspension, typical of South African mine protected vehicles, providing excellent small-arms and mine blast protection.<ref name="defupd">{{cite web|url=http://www.defense-update.com/products/r/RG-31.htm |title=RG-31 Nyala Mine Protected Vehicle |access-date=2011-03-01}}</ref>  The vehicle is designed to resist a blast equivalent to two [[TM-57 mine|TM-57 anti-tank mines]] detonating simultaneously.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/military-identifies-4-of-6-canadian-soldiers-killed-1.652240 |title=Military Identifies 4 of 6 Canadian Soldiers Killed |date=2007-07-04 |access-date=2011-03-01 |work=CBC News}}</ref>  The RG-31 is classified by the [[United States Department of Defense]] as a category 1 [[MRAP|Mine Resistant Ambush Protected]] (MRAP) vehicle.{{citation needed|date=February 2011}}

The vehicle accommodates a crew ranging from 5 to 10 depending on mission needs, depending on model. Dismounting is provided via a large air actuated rear door and two front doors, also air actuated.

In July 2016, the [[Letterkenny Army Depot]] in [[Pennsylvania]] rolled out the latest variant of the RG-31, with improvements including an engine upgrade from 275 to 300&nbsp;hp, a transmission upgrade, independent suspension, 360-degree spotlights for night visibility, and an armored gunner's hatch. The depot is scheduled to produce 929 improved RG-31s through 2020.<ref>[http://armyrecognition.com/july_2016_global_defense_security_news_industry/letterkenny_u.s._army_depot_to_celebrate_production_of_new_rg31_4x4_route_clearance_vehicle_12607161.html Letterkenny U.S. Army Depot to celebrate production of new RG31 4x4 route clearance vehicle] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230909145534/https://armyrecognition.com/july_2016_global_defense_security_news_industry/letterkenny_u.s._army_depot_to_celebrate_production_of_new_rg31_4x4_route_clearance_vehicle_12607161.html |date=9 September 2023 }} - Armyrecognition.com, 26 July 2016</ref>

==Production history==
===Variants===
Variants come in either an [[armoured personnel carrier]] (APC) or utility vehicle (cargo) configuration.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gdlscanada.com/Default.aspx?tabid=206 |title=Basic variant specifications |access-date=19 June 2010 |archive-date=29 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101029013805/http://gdlscanada.com/Default.aspx?tabid=206 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* RG-31 Mk3A &ndash; based on Mamba APC
* RG-31 Mk5<ref>{{cite web |url=http://infodefensa.com/noticias/docs/RG31Mk5_specs%5B1%5D.pdf |title=GDLS RG-31 Mk5 spec sheet PDF |access-date=19 June 2010 |archive-date=1 April 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100401030603/http://infodefensa.com/noticias/docs/RG31Mk5_specs&#91;1&#93;.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* RG-31 Mk5E &ndash; An extended Mk5 with larger passenger/cargo capacity and superior blast and ballistic protection.
* RG-31 Mk5EHM &ndash; An extended GVW version of Mk5E<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Denel OMC RG31 MRAP Family |url=https://militaryvehiclesdata.com/specsheets/land-vehicles/wheeled-armored/4-wheel-armored-vehicles/denel-omc-rg31-family/ |access-date=2025-01-20 |website=militaryvehiclesdata.com |language=en-US}}</ref>
* RG-31 Mk5LHM &ndash; Pick-Op version of Mk5E<ref name=":0" />
* RG-31 Mk5 Ambulance<ref name=":0" />
* RG-31 Mk6E &ndash; Enhanced crew protection
* RG-31 Charger &ndash; US Army version of the Mk3 with a [[Detroit Diesel]] engine and Mk5 with a [[Cummins]] engine
* RG-31M &ndash; features a military wiring harness, central tire inflation and several other new characteristics. This vehicle has a crew of 5.<ref name="defupd"/>
* RG-31 Agrab; [[Mortar carrier]] version with [[SRAMS]] ([[Super Rapid Advanced Mortar System]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.armyrecognition.com/september_2013_defense_industry_military_news_uk/the_bae_systems_rg-31_agrab_120mm_4x4_mortar_carrier_vehicle_to_be_produced_in_uae_2609133.html|title=The BAE Systems RG-31 Agrab 120mm 4x4 mortar carrier vehicle to be produced in UAE 2609133|last=Administrator|website=www.armyrecognition.com|access-date=23 March 2018|archive-date=16 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231216163039/https://armyrecognition.com/september_2013_defense_industry_military_news_uk/the_bae_systems_rg-31_agrab_120mm_4x4_mortar_carrier_vehicle_to_be_produced_in_uae_2609133.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Combat history==
[[File:RG-31 damaged by a mine.jpg|thumb|RG-31 Nyala damaged by a mine]]
[[File:RG31IED.jpg|thumb|RG-31 after getting hit by an [[Improvised explosive device|IED]] in Iraq in 2007. The explosion tore the vehicle in two. The crew survived, but they were severely wounded.]]
*[[Afghanistan]] – Canada, (including 5 leased to Netherlands) ([[International Security Assistance Force|ISAF]]), United States, and Spain<ref>[http://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20110619/54172918062/chacon-afirma-que-el-blindado-evito-un-mal-mayor-en-el-ataque-de-afganistan.html "Chacón afirma que el blindado evitó un "mal mayor" en el ataque de Afganistán"], ''La Vanguardia'', 19 June 2011</ref>
*[[Bosnia and Herzegovina]] – [[UNPROFOR]]
*[[Ethiopia]] / [[Eritrea]] – Canada
*[[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] –- UN
*[[Iraq]] – United States
*[[Colombian conflict|Colombian Armed Conflict]]
*[[Civil war in Côte d'Ivoire|Ivorian Civil War]]
*[[Ivory Coast]] – [[United Nations Operation in Côte d'Ivoire|UNOCI]]
*[[Kosovo]] – [[Kosovo Force|KFOR]]
*[[Lebanon]] – [[United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon|UNIFIL]]
*[[Uganda]] - [[Uganda People's Defence Forces]]
*[[Yemen]] - [[United Arab Emirates]] as part of the [[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]
*[[Mali]] - [[MINUSMA]]
*[[Syria]] - [[UNDOF]], later captured by rebel groups, eventually captured by [[Syrian Army]]{{cn|date=December 2020}}
